title: The `translatable-data-*` attribute

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? ## Problem Statement Localization tools typically examine HTML content for strings that should be localized. These tools typically operate on `Text` nodes in the DOM, and a select subset of specific attributes, such as: * The `alt` attribute on images * The `placeholder` attribute on inputs * The `title` global attribute The html standard lists the [“translatable attributes”](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#translatable-attributes), and the ARIA spec similarly lists its own set of [“translatable attributes”](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#translatable-attributes). However, in some situations, authors will put translatable content into attributes that aren’t included in the lists above. For example: ```html ``` In this case, the text “New”, and the accessible name “Something else” are provided to the user (visually and/or via AT), but are not translated. Another example might be custom element attribute values: ```html ``` In both of these examples, the `data-*` attribute values will not be localized for the user. ## Proposed Solution Introduce a new namespace for attributes, `translatable-data-*`, to address the localization concerns raised above. These would be explicitly listed as [translatable attributes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#translatable-attributes), so that localization tools would know to localize their values. Otherwise, they would function exactly as [custom data attributes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#custom-data-attribute) do today, in that the browser will simply leave them alone. With this solution, the first example above would look like: ```html ```
